standard_prerequisites.name: Contact volume
standard_prerequisites.statement: vol(Y,lambda) is the integral over Y of lambda wedge d lambda, for the contact form lambda on the three-manifold Y.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the left-hand side of the identity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Global surface of section with first return time
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sigma is a global surface of section for the Reeb flow, tau is the first return time and omega is the area form induced by the contact form on Sigma.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects whose integral gives the volume.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reeb flow and the map j
standard_prerequisites.statement: The flow phi of the Reeb vector field sends Sigma x [0,1) onto a full measure subset of Y and satisfies j*(lambda wedge d lambda) = tau ds wedge pr_1^* omega.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the change of variables that turns the integral over Y into an integral over Sigma.

core_obligations: Exhibit the bijection j from Sigma x [0,1) to Sigma x S^1 flowing along the Reeb vector field of the rescaled contact form, and verify that it pulls the volume form back to tau ds wedge pr_1^* omega (source lines 1445-1452).

Use that the restriction of the covering map to the interior of Sigma x S^1 is an alpha-fold branched covering onto a full measure subset of Y, so that the integral of the volume form over Y is the integral of its pull-back divided by alpha (source lines 1453-1454).
Evaluate the resulting integral by integrating first along the S^1 direction, which produces the factor tau, and then over Sigma (source lines 1455-1456).

proof_roadmap.step: Change variables along the Reeb flow and compute the pull-back of the volume form.
Divide by the degree of the branched covering.
Integrate along the circle direction to obtain the integral of the first return time over the section.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 3.5 at source lines 1436-1442: the contact volume of the manifold (Y,lambda) equals 1/alpha times the integral over the section Sigma of the first return time tau against the area form omega. The author's proof (source lines 1444-1458) is a change of variables rather than an estimate: one has to exhibit the flow map j from Sigma times a half-open interval into Sigma times the circle, verify that its pull-back sends lambda wedge d lambda to tau ds wedge pr_1^* omega, and then divide by the number alpha of branches of the covering map restricted to the interior, which is only a full measure condition; the final equality is obtained by integrating first along the circle and then over the section. The statement records neither the flow map nor the covering-degree bookkeeping.
